'''Alexandre Dam Sarr''' ({{IPAc-en|s|ɑːr}} {{respell|SAR}}, {{IPA|fr|alɛksɑ̃dʁ saʁ}}; born 26 April 2005) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Sarr played for the [[France men's national basketball team|French youth national team]] and the [[Perth Wildcats]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) prior to being selected second overall by the Wizards in the [[2024 NBA draft]]. He is the younger brother of basketball player [[Olivier Sarr]].

==Early life==
Sarr was born on 26 April 2005 in [[Bordeaux]], France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2022/player/Alexandre-Dam-Sarr|title=Alexandre Dam SARR|work=fiba.basketball|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509121723/https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2022/player/Alexandre-Dam-Sarr|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Akinsola|first=Luke|url=https://www.nba.com/news/beyond-the-hardwood-france-alex-sarr|title=Beyond the Hardwood: Frenchman Alex Sarr drawing international attention|work=NBA.com|date=21 November 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229141722/https://www.nba.com/news/beyond-the-hardwood-france-alex-sarr|archive-date=29 December 2023}}</ref> He grew up in a family of basketball players, initially in Bordeaux and then later [[Toulouse]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Pantel-Jouve|first=Gabriel|url=https://www.bebasket.fr/alexandre-sarr-va-demarrer-sa-carriere-a-pert-en-australie/|title=Alexandre Sarr va démarrer sa carrière à Perth, en Australie|work=bebasket.fr|date=9 May 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509122708/https://www.bebasket.fr/alexandre-sarr-va-demarrer-sa-carriere-a-pert-en-australie/|archive-date=9 May 2023|language=fr}}</ref> He started playing basketball at the age of four.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xaIPBnMI-kM&ab_channel=PerthWildcats|title=ALEX SARR - We Got Next|work=[[YouTube]]|publisher=[[Perth Wildcats]]|date=22 September 2023|access-date=24 September 2023}}</ref> In 2019, Sarr joined the Spanish club [[Real Madrid Baloncesto]] and played two seasons for their youth team.<ref name=eurohoops>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1224611/ex-real-madrid-prospect-alexandre-sarr-is-the-first-european-signing-of-overtime-elite-league/|title=Ex-Real Madrid prospect Alexandre Sarr is the first European οf Overtime Elite League|work=eurohoops.net|date=1 July 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509123812/https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1224611/ex-real-madrid-prospect-alexandre-sarr-is-the-first-european-signing-of-overtime-elite-league/|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref><ref name=wildcats>{{cite web|url=https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/french-sensation-alexandre-sarr-joins-the-perth-wildcats|title=French sensation Alexandre Sarr joins the Perth Wildcats|work=Wildcats.com|date=9 May 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509002807/https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/french-sensation-alexandre-sarr-joins-the-perth-wildcats|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Overtime Elite (2021–2023)===
In 2021, Sarr moved to the United States to join the newly established [[Overtime Elite]] league in [[Atlanta]], securing him an alternative professional pathway with a guaranteed minimum salary of at least $100,000 per year.<ref name="eurohoops" /><ref name="forbes">{{Cite web |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |date=1 July 2021 |title=Overtime Elite League Signs First European Player In Alexandre Sarr |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/adamzagoria/2021/07/01/overtime-elite-league-signs-first-european-player-in-alexandre-sarr/?sh=4b332c8e60a7 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230509124801/https://www.forbes.com/sites/adamzagoria/2021/07/01/overtime-elite-league-signs-first-european-player-in-alexandre-sarr/?sh=481e102c60a7 |archive-date=9 May 2023 |access-date=28 June 2024 |website=[[Forbes.com]]}}</ref> He played two seasons at Overtime Elite, the first with Team Overtime<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.overtimeelite.com/team-overtime|title=Team Overtime|work=overtimeelite.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220412071353/https://www.overtimeelite.com/team-overtime|archive-date=12 April 2022|access-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> and the second with YNG Dreamerz.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://overtimeelite.com/teams/yng-dreamerz/roster|title=YNG Dreamerz|work=overtimeelite.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20230529123739/https://overtimeelite.com/teams/yng-dreamerz/roster|archive-date=29 May 2023}}</ref> He earned second-team All-OTE honours in 2022–23.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://overtimeelite.com/players/65c5906d-2aed-4c1c-9a11-8fc7a6ba6068|title=Alexandre Sarr|work=overtimeelite.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20230509125604/https://overtimeelite.com/players/65c5906d-2aed-4c1c-9a11-8fc7a6ba6068|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2024–present)===
Sarr declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] on 12 April 2024.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|title=Alex Sarr, projected top-3 pick, declares for 2024 NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/39929335/alex-sarr-projected-top-3-pick-declaring-2024-nba-draft|work=ESPN.com.au|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=13 April 2024|access-date=13 April 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413024352/https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/39929335/alex-sarr-projected-top-3-pick-declaring-2024-nba-draft|archive-date=13 April 2024}}</ref> On 26 June, he was selected second overall by the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref name=":02" /><ref name=":2">{{cite web|first=Noah|last=Trister|title=Washington Wizards take French 7-footer Alex Sarr with the No. 2 pick in the NBA draft|url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-draft-2024-washington-wizards-alex-sarr-cab0a8c1eef551b7189b101232a865bb|work=[[Associated Press]]|date=26 June 2024|access-date=26 June 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240627022929/https://apnews.com/article/nba-draft-2024-washington-wizards-alex-sarr-cab0a8c1eef551b7189b101232a865bb|archive-date=27 June 2024}}</ref> Sarr was picked alongside fellow Frenchmen [[Zaccharie Risacher]] (drafted [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]]) and [[Tidjane Salaün]] (drafted sixth by the [[Charlotte Hornets]]), making France the first foreign nation to have at least three players picked in the top 10 spots of any NBA draft.<ref name=":02" /><ref>{{cite web|first=Gaëtan|last=Delafolie|title=Risacher et Sarr au sommet, Salaün dans le top 10 : draft NBA historique pour la France|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Risacher-n-1-sarr-n-2-draft-nba-historique-pour-la-france/1477805|website=[[L'Équipe]]|date=27 June 2024|access-date=27 June 2024|language=fr-FR}}</ref> On 6 July, he signed his rookie contract with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Wizards Sign First-Rounders Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/wizards-sign-first-rounders-alex-sarr-kyshawn-george.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=6 July 2024|access-date=14 July 2024}}</ref> 

Sarr averaged 5.5 points and 7.8 rebounds in four [[2024 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] games<ref>{{cite web |title=Alex Sarr Player Profile, Washington Wizards - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Alex-Sarr/Summary/162806 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=25 October 2024 |language=en}}</ref> and had two points, five rebounds, one assist, and two blocks in his NBA debut on 24 October.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtics 122-102 Wizards (Oct 24, 2024) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401704639 |website=ESPN |access-date=25 October 2024 |language=en |date=24 October 2024}}</ref> He was named December's [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] Rookie of the Month.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alex Sarr Named Eastern Conference Rookie Of The Month |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/alex-sarr-named-eastern-conference-rookie-of-the-month |website=NBA.com |access-date=3 January 2025}}</ref> On 15 March 2025, he recorded a career-high 34 points, six rebounds and five assists in a 126–123 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]], becoming the youngest player in Wizards' history with a 30-plus-point game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wizards 126-123 Nuggets (Mar 15, 2025) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705541 |access-date=16 March 2025 |work=ESPN |date=15 March 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] and finished fourth in overall Rookie of the Year voting, behind winner [[Stephon Castle]], [[Zaccharie Risacher]], and [[Jaylen Wells]].<ref>{{cite web |date=May 20, 2025  |title=Stephon Castle, Zaccharie Risacher headline NBA All-Rookie First Team |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2024-25-all-rookie-teams-announced |access-date=20 May 2025 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2024-25 NBA Awards Voting |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/awards_2025.html |website=basketball-reference.com |access-date=1 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

Sarr made 48 starts for Washington during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 2.7 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alex Sarr 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5160992/alex-sarr|access-date=July 17, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> On 15 June 2026, Sarr underwent surgery to repair a fractured right foot incurred in an offseason workout. He was expected to be ready for the beginning of the 2026-27 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wizards' Alex Sarr has surgery after fracturing right foot|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49073891/sources-wizards-alex-sarr-surgery-fracturing-foot|access-date=July 17, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
In 2021, Sarr debuted for the [[France men's national under-17 basketball team|French junior national team]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/280331/Alexandre-Dam-Sarr|title=Alexandre Dam Sarr|work=fiba.basketball|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509130645/https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/280331/Alexandre-Dam-Sarr|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> and helped them win the [[2021 FIBA U16 European Challengers|FIBA U16 European Challengers]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Feldman|first=Joseph|url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/7ef19daa-ad67-4e80-947d-8df8303c2d3d|title=Sarr Named to U17 French National Team Select|date=2 May 2022|work=overtimeelite.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509130917/https://overtimeelite.com/articles/7ef19daa-ad67-4e80-947d-8df8303c2d3d|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> He helped France earn bronze at the [[2022 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2022 FIBA U17 World Cup]]<ref name="wildcats" /> and silver at the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2023 FIBA U19 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2023/news/spain-on-top-of-the-world-again-outlast-france-in-otthriller-for-second-title|title=Spain on top of the world again – outlast France in OT thriller for second title|work=fiba.basketball|date=2 July 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703031833/https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2023/news/spain-on-top-of-the-world-again-outlast-france-in-otthriller-for-second-title|archive-date=3 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Woods|first=Dan|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/sarr-s-star-performance-at-world-cup|title=Sarr's Star Performance at World Cup|work=NBL.com.au|date=3 July 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703034307/https://nbl.com.au/news/sarr-s-star-performance-at-world-cup|archive-date=3 July 2023}}</ref>

Sarr joined the [[France men's national basketball team|France senior team]] ahead of the [[EuroBasket 2025]]. On 5 August 2025, he made his national team debut when he scored 20 points on 7-from-10 shooting to lead France to a 81–75 win over [[Montenegro men's national basketball team|Montenegro]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-05 |title=Highlights: Alex Sarr goes off in senior debut for France |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/alex-sarr-goes-off-in-senior-debut-for-france |access-date=2025-09-03 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}}</ref> Sarr played in the first group phase game, but suffered an ankle injury against [[Slovenia men's national basketball team|Slovenia]], which led him to miss the rest of the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-02 |title=Sarr to miss the rest of FIBA EuroBasket 2025 through injury |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/sarr-to-miss-the-rest-of-fiba-eurobasket-2025 |access-date=2025-09-03 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}}</ref>
